content: 1. Mortality Outcomes In the study by Gharebaghi (2020), 14 deaths occurred in the experimental group (29 participants), compared to 6 deaths in the control group (30 participants). The risk ratio (RR) was 2.41 (95% CI: 1.08 to 5.42), indicating a higher risk of mortality in the experimental group. In the study by Raman (2021), no deaths were reported in the experimental group (47 participants), while 1 death occurred in the control group (49 participants). The RR was 0.35 (95% CI: 0.01 to 8.32), suggesting no significant difference. In the study by Tabarsi (2020), 8 deaths occurred in the experimental group (137 participants), compared to 4 deaths in the control group (68 participants). The RR was 0.99 (95% CI: 0.31 to 3.18), showing no significant difference. Overall, the pooled risk ratio for mortality was 1.56 (95% CI: 0.69 to 3.50), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 21%). The test for overall effect was not statistically significant (Z = 1.07, P = 0.28). 2. Need for Mechanical Ventilation In the study by Tabarsi (2020), 21 participants in the experimental group (52 participants) required mechanical ventilation, compared to 10 participants in the control group (32 participants). The RR was 1.29 (95% CI: 0.70 to 2.38), indicating no statistically significant difference. The test for overall effect was not significant (Z = 0.82, P = 0.41). 3. Need for ICU Admission In the study by Tabarsi (2020), 39 participants in the experimental group (52 participants) required ICU admission, compared to 27 participants in the control group (32 participants). The RR was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.72 to 1.10), indicating no significant difference. The test for overall effect was not significant (Z = 1.07, P = 0.29). 4. Duration of Hospitalization (Days) In the study by Gharebaghi (2020), the mean duration of hospitalization was 9 days (SD: 4.44) in the experimental group (29 participants) and 7 days (SD: 2.22) in the control group (30 participants). The mean difference (MD) was 2.00 days (95% CI: 0.20 to 3.80). In the study by Raman (2021), the mean duration of hospitalization was 7.72 days (SD: 2.69) in the experimental group (47 participants) and 17.5 days (SD: 5.01) in the control group (46 participants). The MD was -9.78 days (95% CI: -11.42 to -8.14). In the study by Tabarsi (2020), the mean duration of hospitalization was 8.5 days (SD: 4.44) in the experimental group (52 participants) and 5.5 days (SD: 2.96) in the control group (32 participants). The MD was 3.00 days (95% CI: 1.42 to 4.58). The pooled MD was -1.60 days (95% CI: -9.77 to 6.58), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 99%). The test for overall effect was not significant (Z = 0.38, P = 0.70). 5. Duration of Mechanical Ventilation (Days) In the study by Raman (2021), the mean duration of mechanical ventilation was 2.42 days (SD: 0.9) in the experimental group (12 participants) and 4.47 days (SD: 2.7) in the control group (19 participants). The MD was -2.05 days (95% CI: -3.37 to -0.73). The test for overall effect was statistically significant (Z = 3.05, P = 0.002). 6. Duration of Stay in ICU (Days) In the study by Gharebaghi (2020), the mean duration of ICU stay was 4 days (SD: 2.22) in the experimental group (29 participants) and 3 days (SD: 1.48) in the control group (30 participants). The MD was 1.00 day (95% CI: 0.03 to 1.97). In the study by Raman (2021), the mean duration of ICU stay was 4 days (SD: 1.4) in the experimental group (2 participants) and 5 days (SD: 3) in the control group (3 participants). The MD was -1.00 day (95% CI: -4.91 to 2.91). In the study by Tabarsi (2020), the mean duration of ICU stay was 5 days (SD: 2.96) in the experimental group (52 participants) and 4 days (SD: 3.7) in the control group (32 participants). The MD was 1.00 day (95% CI: -0.51 to 2.51). The pooled MD was 0.92 days (95% CI: 0.12 to 1.71), with no heterogeneity (I² = 0%). The test for overall effect was statistically significant (Z = 2.25, P = 0.02).
